newsitem.title: UK: Britain leaves drug pricing scheme unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Britain leaves drug pricing scheme unchanged.

text.p: Britain's drug pricing scheme, which limits drug company profits on their sales of branded medicines to the National Health Service, is to remain unchanged, the Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry (ABPI) said on Friday.
In their mid-term review of the pricing scheme, the ABPI and the Department of Health had decided to keep target profitability at the current range of 17 to 21 percent return on capital.
The ABPI said measures would come into force this year and next to adress "export disincentives" in the pricing system, known as the Pharmaceutical Price Regulation Scheme (PPRS).
The disincentives come into play when a drugs firm raises exports, which artificially increase in profitability under the PPRS because the allocation of UK home costs are reduced.
The current PPRS will remain in force until October 1998.
